summary: The main article describes a visible-light-mediated direct deoxygenation of aromatic carboxylic acids for ketone synthesis. It includes 1 table for optimization, 9 figures illustrating substrate scopes, functional group compatibility, synthetic applications (including zolpidem synthesis), and mechanistic studies.

items.heading: Fig. 1
items.caption: Applications of aromatic carboxylic acids in organic synthesis. a The nature choice of aromatic carboxylic acid. b Known ketone synthesis from acids (indirect strategies). c This work: direct deoxygenative C -C coupling by visible light
items.description: This figure compares traditional indirect strategies for ketone synthesis from carboxylic acids with the direct deoxygenative approach developed in this work.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of reaction conditions
items.description: This table summarizes the screening of photocatalysts, bases, and reagents to optimize the yield of the deoxygenative C-C coupling reaction.

items.heading: Fig. 2
items.caption: Aromatic carboxylic acid scope. Bn benzyl; Boc tert -butoxycarbonyl; Ts para -toluenesulfonyl
items.description: This figure displays the variety of aromatic and heteroaromatic carboxylic acids that are compatible with the deoxygenative ketone synthesis.

items.heading: Fig. 3
items.caption: Alkene scope
items.description: This figure illustrates the broad range of alkenes, including vinylpyridines, styrenes, and electron-deficient alkenes, used in the reaction.

items.heading: Fig. 4
items.caption: Examining functional group compatibility. Reaction conditions: photocatalyst I (1 mol%), 1a (0.1 mmol, 1.0 equiv.), 2a (0.15 mmol, 1.5 equiv.), Ph3P (0.12 mmol, 1.2 equiv.), biomolecules, pH 7.4 PBS buffer/DCM (1:1, 2.0 mL), blue LEDs, 25 °C
items.description: This figure demonstrates the robustness of the reaction in the presence of various biomolecules like amino acids and DNA.

items.heading: Fig. 5
items.caption: Synthetic application. a Late-stage application in the complex molecules. b Synthesis of zolpidem
items.description: This figure shows the application of the method for late-stage functionalization of drugs and the total synthesis of zolpidem.

items.heading: Fig. 6
items.caption: Deoxygenative macrocyclization in the synthesis of cyclophanebraced cycloketones
items.description: This figure depicts the use of the deoxygenative coupling for the construction of large macrocyclic ketones.

items.heading: Fig. 7
items.caption: Downstream transformations
items.description: This figure shows how the synthesized ketones can be converted into various nitrogen-containing heterocyclic compounds.

items.heading: Fig. 8
items.caption: Mechanistic studies. a Control experiments with additives. b Radical cyclization experiment. c Deuterium-labeling experiments. d 18 O-labeling experiments. e Aromatic carboxylate anion as substrate. f Proposed mechanism
items.description: This figure details the experimental evidence and the proposed catalytic cycle for the deoxygenative coupling reaction.

items.heading: Fig. 9
items.caption: A three-component reductive coupling reaction
items.description: This figure presents an extension of the methodology to a three-component coupling of acids, amines, and aldehydes to form alpha-amino ketones.
